_what: Every look-ahead scenario that is not a check's Pass / Fail shape, as the fixture that makes it and the markers that must come out. THE DEFINITION, not a description of one: tools/GameHarness turns each suite into an in-game run, and tests/scenario_suites.rs puts the same scenarios to the engine over the shipped index. Adding a suite adds a test to both; neither side declares anything of its own.
_why_a_suite_and_not_a_row: A suite is what fixes a launch. The mod reads the global state file once, when it first needs it, and BepInEx reads its configuration at chainload - so scenarios that disagree about either cannot share a game, however much else they have in common. What can vary inside a suite is the save, which the probe loads in place, and the conversation, which it opens on command.
_markers: none = nothing reachable outranks the option itself, orange = it can still reach a line no save has read, red = it can still reach a line this save has not read, gaveUp = the search ran out before it could say. The mod's own rule, which both executors apply: an option that is itself unseen anywhere is never marked, since nothing outranks the top rung.
_policies: markers is one of named - the listed options must match and every other option in the menu must be unmarked - noneAnywhere, for a menu whose option ids are not known until it has been opened, and ignored, where the markers are not the subject. branches is ignored, noneAnywhere, or everyCheck with a pass and a fail half; see branch-shapes.json for what a half may hold.
_stops: Every menu a scenario is held to is a stop: what to press to reach it, and what it must show. A scenario of one menu names one stop, and nothing about a menu is said outside the list - there is one shape rather than a first menu written one way and the rest another. A second stop presses on from where the last was checked: in game the conversation carries on in place with no reload, and offline the stop is walked from the conversation's start with every earlier stop's inputs in front of its own, which is the same walk. FOR ONE WALK PASSING THE SAME GROUND, and nothing else: a later stop sees a world the earlier stops moved, so two claims that each want the same known starting world are two scenarios, whatever the second load costs. The pair this exists for is manana-commuhub, where the question IS whether a menu answers the same on first arrival as it does after a loop back to it.
_two_files: This one and branch-shapes.json, and the split is by SHAPE rather than by executor. A branch shape varies along one axis - what the two outcomes of one check land on - so its definition is a table with the conversation and entry named once and eight rows under them, and the eight-shape coverage argument is only readable in that form. Everything else varies along all of them at once, so it is written out. Both are shared definitions and both build the same in-game suite type.
_offline_only: A scenario marked offlineOnly is run by tests/scenario_suites.rs and skipped by the in-game harness. WHAT IT IS FOR, and the only thing it is for: a row that repeats another row of the same suite in the GAME while covering a different group OFFLINE. The offline executor asks a suite's claim of every entry in a group, so a second conversation is a second group covered and costs milliseconds; the in-game run loads a save for it, five or six seconds, to watch the same rule hold in a menu the first row already watched it hold in. A row that stages a different balance, a different recorded state, or a check where the first had none is NOT this - that is the feature, and both executors run it.
_executor_specific: What only one side can run goes under a key naming the executor, offline or inGame, rather than in a scenario's own fields - a definition that reads as shared and is not is worse than two honest declarations. Two standing cases. inGame: the artefact and log checks, which read files the game wrote over a whole launch, are C# predicates, and are named here and resolved there; and notInDefaultRun, the reason a suite stays out of the default in-game run - every suite is in it unless it gives one, and the offline executor runs them all. offline: a claim about EVERY entry in a group rather than about the options a menu happened to compose, which no in-game run can make because a menu is all it can see.
_what_is_not_here: 1. switched-off: What it stages is a MOD SETTING - MarkLookAhead=false - and there is no such thing to stage without a mod: the offline engine has no switch to turn off, so from the same fixture it answers what the money suite answers, one option marked. A row claiming every option is unmarked would be a definition only one side could execute. It stays declared in LookAheadSuites, honestly, and the remarks there say the same. 2. engine-recovery: tests in-game notification when the rust look-ahead process dies, and we respawn.  3. engine-death: tests in-game notification when the rust look-ahead process dies, and we give up.

suites.what: the biggest conversations cost nothing when every entry is already recorded
suites.why: This suite used to be called headroom and used to be a measurement: the staged global state records every entry of every conversation, which was once the most expensive shape a crawl could take, because no option's own novelty is unseen-anywhere - so the early exit did not fire - and nothing reachable is unseen-anywhere either, so a crawl could not stop the instant it found something and had to explore everything. The no-potential-improvement short-circuit ended that: when every entry is recorded, nothing can outrank the option being asked about, so no walk can produce a marker and the crawl is skipped before any state is built. The expensive shape is now the near-opposite - a group with one unseen node, or a handful - and is measured elsewhere. What these five conversations are for now is the strongest available statement of the cheap case: they are the largest in the game, so if a crawl were going to run anywhere it would run here, and the claim is that not one does. FIVE OFFLINE AND ONE IN GAME. The claim is asked of every entry of all five groups by tests/scenario_suites.rs, which is where it is worth having five; the suite says nothing about markers - its policy is ignored - so the game has only one thing to show, and Joyce, the largest of them, shows it.
suites._size: The five are ranks two to six of the game's 1,501 conversations by entry count - 368, 14, 631, 28 and 1030, from 1,770 entries down to 1,476 - and tests/all_seen.rs holds them to that against the shipped index rather than taking it on trust. The largest, 362, is not among them. ENTRY COUNT IS NOT THE COST: the budget counts entry-and-state pairs, so what blows up is the state slots a conversation touches multiplied by its reachable entries, and the count turns out to be a poor proxy - 1030 is the sixth largest and its crawls peak at 201 states, a thousandth of Joyce's. It is still the only ordering available without running them.
suites.settingsWhy: Kept on so that a crawl WOULD leave a trace. The claim is that the files say nothing happened; that means nothing unless the run was configured to write them.

The engine cuts what a walk has passed since its current hub, so the row WALKS from the conversation's start rather than naming the menu, and only 399 keeps its star. The global state is the player's own, which is what decides which lines no save has read.

suites.what: a menu in a group the clock moves through is answered in the game, with the register carried
suites.why: de-086x: the carried clock is checked offline three ways and the plugin sends the lock, but no in-game run had ever built a search state in a group that carries a clock - so the deployed host binary, where the budget, the threading and the process boundary all differ from a test, had never run the layout the register lives in. 631's group is one of the nine carriers, and with this save's world - unlocked, 15:00 on day three - its layout takes a seven-bit clock with a ceiling of 95 quarter-hour steps. A LOCKED CLOCK WOULD CARRY NO BITS AT ALL, which is why the save matters as much as the group. at-evart rather than at-joyce, and an empty global state rather than the recorded one, because a menu where everything is recorded is settled before a diagram is built: this save has been through Joyce's hub, so four of its seven options sit on the bottom rung with unread content behind them and the menu discriminates. WHAT THE MARKERS ARE DOING HERE is holding the answer to the same standard as every other suite - the clock is what the run is for, but a run that only counted diagram nodes could carry the register and still answer wrongly.
